newsitem.title: UK: Land sale may help fund Channel rail link - report.
newsitem.headline: Land sale may help fund Channel rail link - report.

text.p: Britain's Labour government may allow London and Continental Railways (LCR), which is building the Channel Tunnel Rail Link (CTRL), to sell state-owned land near King's Cross station and in east London to help fund the project, the Guardian said on Wednesday.
A spokeswoman for the Department of Transport had no comment on the report.
The Guardian said about 35 acres of development land near King's Cross and a further 120 acres in Stratford, east London, could be sold as long as the money was spent to fund the link.
LCR had already been promised 1.4 billion pounds ($2.2 billion) in subsidies from public money for the project and had pledged to contribute two billion pounds itself, the newspaper said.
LCR won the contract to develop the three billion pound venture from the previous Conservative government last February.
The LCR consortium comprises National Express Group Plc, the Virgin Group, SBC Warburg, London Electricity Plc which is owned by U.S. group Entergy, and engineering group Bechtel.
LCR, which does not get paid until the job is almost done, was planning a stock market flotation and major debt issue to raise the cash for building the link.
Preparatory engineering work on the 100 km link began in June and five major tunnelling contracts worth 800 million pounds were put out to tender.
